key_insight: Incorporating estimated depth into thermal 3D Gaussian Splatting significantly improves novel-view quality and rendering efficiency by guiding splat placement and reducing unnecessary multimodal fusion overhead.
problem_solved: Fusion of thermal imagery with RGB or other sensors for 3D Gaussian Splatting is often slow, noisy, and computationally expensive; the paper addresses how to make thermal-based novel-view synthesis more accurate and efficient without heavy multimodal pipelines.
method: Estimate depth maps from thermal inputs (or jointly from available modalities) and use them to initialize and anchor 3D Gaussian splats.
Apply depth-guided pruning and importance weighting to reduce the number of splats and focus optimization on geometrically consistent regions.
Optimize a lightweight fusion/ rendering pipeline that leverages depth priors to speed training/ rendering while preserving thermal-specific appearance.
impact: Makes thermal-aware 3D reconstruction and novel-view synthesis practical for real-time or resource-constrained applications (e.g., robotics, autonomous driving, search-and-rescue), improving robustness in low-visibility conditions while lowering compute requirements.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: thermal image → depth estimator → depth-guided Gaussian splat generation → rendered novel view
Before/after comparisons: novel-view thermal renderings with and without depth guidance (side-by-side)
Bar/line chart: quality (e.g., PSNR/LPIPS) and rendering time trade-off showing speedup and accuracy gain
Icon set: thermal camera, depth map overlay, lightweight GPU/clock to represent efficiency gains
paper_title: Supercharging Thermal Gaussian Splatting with Depth Estimation
paper_authors: Manoj Biswanath, Chenxin Cai, Hannah Schieber, Daniel Roth, Benjamin Busam
